Hi Jane — thanks for the files, they were helpful. See inline below and a concise punchlist we use for private deployments. I'll book a 30-min intake call after we confirm owners.

Onboarding punchlist (what Redwood needs before scheduling smoke run):
1) Account & billing: signed MAU addendum / purchase order (we'll send DocuSign link).
2) Network: primary VPC CID blocks, transit/peering diagram (we got your diagram — will review), IP allowlist for egress, and firewall rule owners.
3) Identity & access: dedicated service account emails, recommended least-privilege IAM roles, and SSH bastion owner.
4) KMS & keys: KMS provider (cloud KMS / HSM) details, key rotation policy, and keystore access process (we require pull-only key access for secrets staging).
5) Logging & audit: retention requirements, syslog/ELK endpoint for forwarding (if applicable), and required evidence for SOC2 scoping.
6) Evidence artifacts: SOC2 summary (we have), encryption-at-rest attestations, network segmentation diagrams, and an ops contact list for escalation.
7) Ports & endpoints: list of outbound ports your network will permit to Redwood control plane, and any proxy requirements.
8) Test accounts: a small set of test credentials or ephemeral tokens and a technical point-of-contact for 1st-day troubleshooting.
9) Runbook & smoke criteria: agreed success criteria for the smoke run (tokenized test workload, latency thresholds, and request throughput for the validation window).

I'll attach our standard punchlist workbook for completion — please send back the populated sheet and any outstanding artifacts. We typically ask for 3 business days to review artifacts before a smoke run so week-of-May 6 is tight but possible if we get materials by Monday morning.

Attachments referenced: redwood_private_onboard_punchlist_v1.xlsx
